title: Beef rendang
summary: Slow-cooked beef infused with coconut milk, lemongrass, galangal and spices until dark and caramelised.
method: Blend the shallots, garlic, ginger, chillies and ground coriander with a splash of water until coarse. Cut the beef into 4 cm cubes.
Heat the oil in a heavy pot over medium heat. Fry the paste until fragrant and darker, then add the lemongrass and lime leaves until aromatic.
Add the beef, coconut milk and salt. Bring to a simmer, then lower the heat.
Cook uncovered or partly covered for 2 hours, stirring more often as the liquid reduces, until the beef is tender.
Keep cooking gently for about 25 minutes until the sauce thickens and clings to the meat. Stop when the paste is deep brown and the beef pulls apart easily.

stages.title: Blend the spice paste
steps: Blend shallots, garlic, ginger, chillies and coriander with a splash of water until coarse.
Pat beef dry and cut into equal 4 cm cubes for even cooking.

stages.title: Fry the aromatics
steps: Heat oil in a heavy pot and fry the paste over medium heat until fragrant and darker.
Add lemongrass and lime leaves, stirring until their aromas release.

stages.title: Slow-cook the beef
steps: Add beef, coconut milk and salt; bring to a simmer and lower the heat.
Cook uncovered or partly covered for 2 hours, stirring more often as liquid reduces, until beef is tender.

stages.title: Reduce to a coating
steps: Continue cooking gently until the coconut mixture thickens and clings to the meat.
Stir frequently to prevent burning and stop when the paste is deep brown and the beef pulls apart easily.

tips: Rendang is a slow reduction, not a soupy curry.
Stir frequently during the final 30 minutes as coconut solids can scorch.
variations: Add a pinch of chilli flakes for extra heat.
Finish with fresh herbs or citrus where appropriate.
storage: Refrigerate promptly in an airtight container for up to 3 days. Reheat cooked components until steaming hot; keep crisp garnishes separate.

title: Quiche Lorraine
summary: Buttery pastry filled with smoky bacon, Gruyère and a delicate savoury egg custard.
method: Heat the oven to 190°C. Press the pastry into a 23 cm tart tin, line with baking paper and weights, and bake 15 minutes. Remove the weights and bake 5 minutes more.
Fry the bacon in a dry pan over medium heat until lightly golden and the fat has rendered. Drain on kitchen paper.
Whisk the eggs, cream, milk, nutmeg and pepper until just combined, without making it foamy.
Scatter the bacon and Gruyère over the baked pastry case, then pour in the custard.
Bake at 180°C for 30–35 minutes, until the edges are set and the centre just wobbles.
Rest for 10 minutes before slicing.

stages.title: Blind-bake pastry
steps: Heat oven to 190°C conventional and press pastry into a 23 cm tart tin.
Line with baking paper and weights, bake 15 minutes, then remove weights and bake 5 minutes more.

stages.title: Cook bacon
steps: Fry bacon in a dry pan over medium heat until lightly golden and fat renders.
Drain on kitchen paper so the filling does not become greasy.

stages.title: Make the custard
steps: Whisk eggs, cream, milk, nutmeg and pepper until just combined, avoiding excessive foam.
Scatter bacon and cheese evenly over the baked pastry case.

stages.title: Bake and rest
steps: Pour custard into the tart and bake at 180°C for 30–35 minutes until edges are set and centre gently wobbles.
Rest 10 minutes before slicing so the custard firms without drying.

tips: Avoid overbaking: the centre should still have a slight wobble.
Classic Lorraine often omits cheese; Gruyère is a popular addition.
variations: Add a pinch of chilli flakes for extra heat.
Finish with fresh herbs or citrus where appropriate.
storage: Refrigerate promptly in an airtight container for up to 3 days. Reheat cooked components until steaming hot; keep crisp garnishes separate.

title: Teriyaki chicken donburi
summary: Tender teriyaki-glazed chicken over steamed rice with spring onions and sesame.
method: Rinse the rice until the water runs nearly clear, then cook it over low heat with the packet amount of water. Rest covered for 10 minutes and fluff.
Stir the soy sauce, mirin, sake (or water) and brown sugar until the sugar dissolves. Thinly slice the spring onions.
Heat the oil in a skillet over medium-high heat. Cook the chicken thighs 5–6 minutes each side, until the thickest part reaches 75°C.
Pour the sauce into the pan and simmer, turning the chicken, until glossy and lightly thickened.
Slice the chicken and spoon it over the rice with the pan glaze. Top with spring onions and sesame seeds.

stages.title: Cook the rice
steps: Rinse rice until the water runs nearly clear and cook over low heat with the packet-specified amount of water.
Rest covered for 10 minutes after cooking, then fluff with a fork.

stages.title: Mix the glaze
steps: Stir soy sauce, mirin, sake and sugar until the sugar dissolves.
Slice spring onions thinly and keep the green tops for serving.

stages.title: Sear chicken
steps: Heat oil in a skillet and cook thighs over medium-high heat for 5–6 minutes each side.
Check the thickest part reaches 75°C before removing excess rendered fat.

stages.title: Glaze and serve
steps: Pour sauce into the pan and simmer, turning chicken, until glossy and lightly thickened.
Slice chicken and spoon over rice with pan glaze, spring onions and sesame seeds.

tips: Pat the chicken thighs dry before they hit the pan: surface moisture steams the meat instead of searing it, so you miss the browned edges that give the glaze something to cling to.
Spoon off excess rendered fat before adding the sauce, as thigh fat will keep the glaze from thickening and leave it greasy rather than glossy.
Add the sauce only once the chicken is cooked through and simmer briefly: the sugar and mirin caramelise fast and can turn bitter and sticky if they reduce for too long on high heat.
variations: Swap the chicken for salmon fillets, searing skin-side down for about 4 minutes, then flipping and glazing for the last 2 minutes so the fish stays moist.
Make it a veggie-loaded bowl by adding steamed broccolini and quick-pickled cucumber on the side, and top with a soft-boiled egg for extra protein for the kids.
storage: Refrigerate promptly in an airtight container for up to 3 days. Reheat cooked components until steaming hot; keep crisp garnishes separate.

title: Beef bulgogi
summary: Thinly sliced beef marinated in soy, pear, garlic and sesame, quickly seared until caramelised.
method: Mix the soy sauce, brown sugar, grated pear, garlic, ginger and sesame oil. Toss through the sliced beef and refrigerate for at least 20 minutes.
Slice the onion into fine half-moons and cut the spring onions into 4 cm pieces. Drain the excess marinade from the beef so it sears.
Heat the neutral oil in a large frying pan over high heat until very hot.
Cook the beef in small batches for 2–3 minutes per side, until browned and cooked through.
Return all the beef to the pan with the onion and spring onions. Toss until the onion softens slightly.
Serve straight away with rice and lettuce leaves, if using.

stages.title: Make the marinade
steps: Mix soy sauce, sugar, grated pear, garlic, ginger and sesame oil until combined.
Toss with thinly sliced beef and refrigerate for at least 20 minutes.

stages.title: Prepare vegetables
steps: Slice onion into fine half-moons and cut spring onions into 4 cm pieces.
Drain excess marinade from beef so it sears rather than boils.

stages.title: Sear in batches
steps: Heat a large skillet until very hot and add a little neutral oil.
Cook beef in small batches for 2–3 minutes per side until browned and fully cooked.

stages.title: Finish and serve
steps: Return beef to pan with onion and spring onion, tossing until onion softens slightly.
Serve immediately with rice and optional lettuce leaves.

tips: Freeze the beef for about 30 minutes before slicing so you can cut it paper-thin; thin slices cook in seconds and stay tender.
Grated pear contains enzymes that tenderise the beef, but marinate for no more than 4 hours or the meat turns mushy.
Cook in small batches in a very hot pan; crowding drops the temperature so the beef steams and turns grey instead of caramelising.
variations: Swap the beef for thinly sliced pork shoulder (dwaeji bulgogi) and add 1 tbsp gochujang to the marinade for a spicy, sticky version.
Serve as lettuce wraps (ssam) with steamed rice, kimchi and ssamjang, so everyone builds their own at the table.
storage: Refrigerate promptly in an airtight container for up to 3 days. Reheat cooked components until steaming hot; keep crisp garnishes separate.

title: Moroccan chicken tagine with olives
summary: Chicken gently braised with olives, preserved lemon and aromatic Moroccan spices.
method: Heat the olive oil in a casserole over medium-high heat. Brown the seasoned chicken thighs for 3–4 minutes per side until deep golden, then set aside.
Reduce to medium-low and cook the sliced onion until soft, scraping up the browned bits. Stir in the garlic, ginger, turmeric and cumin for 30 seconds until fragrant.
Return the chicken to the pan with the stock, bring to a simmer and cover. Cook 30–35 minutes until tender and 75°C in the thickest part.
Rinse and finely slice the preserved lemon rind. Stir it in with the olives and simmer uncovered until the sauce lightly thickens, then finish with coriander.

stages.title: Brown chicken
steps: Heat olive oil in a casserole over medium-high heat and season chicken lightly.
Brown thighs on both sides for 3–4 minutes per side until deep golden, then transfer to a plate without cooking through.

stages.title: Soften aromatics
steps: Lower heat and cook onion until softened, scraping up browned bits.
Add garlic, ginger, turmeric and cumin and stir for 30 seconds until fragrant.

stages.title: Braise gently
steps: Return chicken with stock, bring to a simmer and cover.
Cook 30–35 minutes until tender and the thickest part reaches 75°C.

stages.title: Add preserved lemon
steps: Rinse preserved lemon and finely slice the rind; discard excess pulp and seeds.
Stir in olives and lemon rind, simmer uncovered until sauce lightly thickens, then finish with coriander.

tips: Brown the thighs well before braising: the caramelised bits left in the pot dissolve into the stock and give the sauce a deeper, roasted flavour.
Rinse the preserved lemon and use only the rind, because the salty pulp can make the whole tagine harsh and over-salted, especially once the sauce reduces.
Add the olives and lemon rind only at the end, as long simmering turns the olives bitter and dulls the bright, fragrant lemon flavour.
variations: Swap the green olives for a handful of dried apricots or prunes and add a cinnamon stick with the spices for a sweeter, more Fez-style tagine.

Make it with lamb shoulder pieces instead of chicken, extending the covered braise to about 1.5 hours until the meat is fork-tender, and stir through a can of drained chickpeas for the last 15 minutes.
storage: Refrigerate promptly in an airtight container for up to 3 days. Reheat cooked components until steaming hot; keep crisp garnishes separate.

title: Chicken enchiladas rojas
summary: Soft tortillas rolled around spiced chicken and baked under red chilli sauce and melted cheese.
method: Heat the oil in a skillet over medium heat and soften the diced onion until translucent, about 4 minutes.
Stir in the shredded chicken and 100 ml of the enchilada sauce until steaming hot.
Warm the tortillas in a dry skillet over medium heat until pliable, then spread a thin layer of sauce over a baking dish.
Divide the chicken mixture between the tortillas, roll up and place seam-side down in the dish.
Pour over the remaining sauce and scatter with the cheese.
Bake at 190°C for 18–22 minutes until bubbling and hot throughout. Rest 5 minutes, then top with sour cream and coriander.

stages.title: Prepare filling
steps: Heat oil in a skillet over medium heat and soften diced onion until translucent.
Stir in shredded chicken and 100 ml enchilada sauce, heating until steaming hot.

stages.title: Soften tortillas
steps: Heat tortillas briefly in a dry skillet so they roll without cracking.
Spread a thin layer of sauce across the base of a baking dish.

stages.title: Fill and roll
steps: Divide chicken mixture between tortillas, roll tightly and arrange seam-side down.
Pour remaining sauce over the top and scatter with grated cheese.

stages.title: Bake and serve
steps: Bake at 190°C conventional for 18–22 minutes until bubbling and hot throughout.
Rest 5 minutes, then top with sour cream and coriander.

tips: Warm the corn tortillas in a dry pan before rolling: cold corn tortillas crack and split, while warmed ones turn pliable and hold the filling.
Spread a thin layer of sauce on the base of the dish first so the tortillas don't stick or scorch, and the bottom ones soften into the sauce rather than drying out.
Shred the cheese yourself from a block of Monterey Jack: pre-grated bags contain anti-caking agents that stop it melting into a smooth, bubbly blanket.
variations: Swap the chicken for a filling of black beans and roasted sweet potato with the same red sauce for a vegetarian version that still holds together when rolled.
Make enchiladas verdes by replacing the red sauce with salsa verde and topping with crumbled queso fresco instead of the Monterey Jack, for a tangier, lighter finish.
storage: Refrigerate promptly in an airtight container for up to 3 days. Reheat cooked components until steaming hot; keep crisp garnishes separate.

title: Char siu pork
summary: Sticky Cantonese-style roast pork glazed with honey, hoisin and fragrant five-spice.
ingredients: 800 g pork shoulder, cut into strips
method: Whisk the hoisin, soy, honey, Shaoxing wine, five-spice, garlic and brown sugar into a glaze. Set 2 tablespoons aside in a clean bowl for basting.
Coat the pork strips in the remaining glaze and refrigerate for at least 30 minutes, or overnight.
Heat the oven to 200°C. Arrange the pork on a rack over a foil-lined tray and roast for 25 minutes, turning halfway.
Brush with the reserved glaze and roast until the pork is cooked through and tender.
Increase the oven to 220°C for a few minutes until the edges are sticky and lightly charred. Rest for 5 minutes, then slice across the grain.

stages.title: Mix marinade
steps: Whisk hoisin, soy, honey, wine, five-spice, garlic and sugar into a smooth glaze.
Reserve 2 tablespoons in a separate clean bowl for basting before adding raw meat.

stages.title: Marinate pork
steps: Coat pork strips thoroughly and refrigerate at least 30 minutes, ideally overnight.
Arrange on a rack above a foil-lined roasting tray so hot air circulates.

stages.title: Roast the pork
steps: Heat oven to 200°C conventional and roast 25 minutes, turning halfway.
Brush with reserved clean glaze and continue cooking until pork is safely cooked and tender.

stages.title: Caramelise and rest
steps: Increase oven to 220°C for a few minutes until edges become sticky and lightly charred.
Rest pork 5 minutes before slicing across the grain.

tips: Use pork shoulder (or scotch fillet) rather than lean loin: the marbling bastes the meat as it roasts, so the strips stay juicy instead of drying out under the high heat.
Roast on a rack over a foil-lined tray with a splash of water in the tray: air circulates so the glaze caramelises on all sides, and the water stops the dripping sugars from burning and smoking.

Keep the reserved glaze separate from the raw meat and only brush it on for the final stage: it gives a fresh, glossy layer of stickiness that the first coat loses to the oven, and it avoids cross-contamination.
variations: Swap the pork shoulder for chicken thigh fillets and cut the roasting time to about 20 minutes: the same glaze gives a quicker, milder char siu that suits younger kids.
Add 1 tbsp of red fermented bean curd to the marinade for a more traditional Cantonese flavour and a deeper reddish colour, without needing food dye.
storage: Refrigerate promptly in an airtight container for up to 3 days. Reheat cooked components until steaming hot; keep crisp garnishes separate.

title: Butter chicken
summary: Tender tandoori-spiced chicken in a buttery tomato cream sauce with warming spices.
method: Mix the yoghurt, half the garam masala, paprika, half the garlic and the salt. Coat the chicken and marinate in the fridge for at least 20 minutes.
Melt 20 g butter in a wide pan over medium-high heat. Sear the chicken in batches until lightly coloured, then set aside (it finishes in the sauce).
Add the remaining butter, garlic, ginger and tomato paste, and cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add the passata and remaining garam masala. Simmer for 15 minutes, blending if you want a silky sauce.
Return the chicken and juices and simmer until it reaches 75°C. Reduce the heat, stir in the cream and season with salt.
Serve with rice, if using.

stages.title: Marinate chicken
steps: Mix yoghurt, half the garam masala, paprika, half the garlic and salt.
Coat chicken and refrigerate for at least 20 minutes before cooking.

stages.title: Sear the chicken
steps: Heat 20 g butter in a wide pan over medium-high heat and cook chicken in batches until lightly coloured.
Remove to a plate; the chicken will finish cooking in the sauce.

stages.title: Build the sauce
steps: Add remaining butter, garlic, ginger and tomato paste; stir for 1 minute.
Add passata and remaining garam masala, simmer 15 minutes and blend carefully if a silky sauce is preferred.

stages.title: Finish gently
steps: Return chicken and juices, simmer until chicken reaches 75°C.
Reduce heat, stir in cream and taste for salt before serving with rice.

tips: Use thighs rather than breast: the extra fat keeps the chicken juicy through the sear and the long simmer, and it won't turn stringy like breast can.
Sear the chicken in batches so the pan stays hot; crowding it steams the meat, and you lose the browned bits that add depth to the sauce.
Stir the cream in off a low heat, not a rolling simmer, so the sauce stays smooth and doesn't split from the acidity of the passata.
variations: Swap the cream for coconut cream for a dairy-free-style sauce with a slightly sweeter, rounder flavour.
Make it with 600 g firm paneer or peeled prawns instead of chicken, adding prawns in the last 4 minutes so they stay tender.
storage: Refrigerate promptly in an airtight container for up to 3 days. Reheat cooked components until steaming hot; keep crisp garnishes separate.

title: Spanish chicken and chorizo rice
summary: One-pan saffron-tinted rice with juicy chicken, smoky chorizo and sweet peppers.
method: Heat the olive oil in a wide pan over medium-high heat. Brown the seasoned chicken for about 5 minutes, then add the sliced chorizo and cook until it releases its red oil. Transfer both to a plate.
In the same pan over medium heat, soften the onion and capsicum for about 5 minutes. Add the garlic and smoked paprika and cook until fragrant.
Stir in the tomatoes and rice until the grains are well coated.

Pour in the hot stock with the saffron and return the chicken and chorizo. Simmer gently over medium-low heat without stirring for 18 to 22 minutes, adding a little hot water only if the rice dries out before it's tender.
Check the chicken reaches 75°C and the rice is tender. Cover off the heat for 5 minutes, then fluff lightly to keep the golden crust.

stages.title: Brown the proteins
steps: Heat olive oil in a wide pan over medium-high heat and brown seasoned chicken pieces for about 5 minutes, until golden.
Add sliced chorizo and cook until its paprika-red oil releases, then transfer both to a plate.

stages.title: Build the rice base
steps: Soften onion and capsicum in the same pan over medium heat for about 5 minutes, until soft, then add garlic and smoked paprika.
Stir in tomatoes and rice, coating grains in the fragrant oil.

stages.title: Simmer without stirring
steps: Pour in hot stock infused with saffron and return chicken and chorizo.
Simmer gently without stirring for 18–22 minutes, adding a little hot water only if rice dries before tender.

stages.title: Rest and serve
steps: Check chicken reaches 75°C and rice is cooked; cover off the heat for 5 minutes.
Fluff only lightly at serving to preserve any golden crust underneath.

tips: Brown the chicken thighs skin-side down first and leave them alone: the rendered fat and caramelised bits left in the pan flavour the rice, so don't wipe it out.
Use raw cooking chorizo, not the dry cured kind: it releases paprika-red oil that stains and seasons every grain, while cured chorizo stays firm and gives far less flavour to the rice.
Don't stir once the stock is in: leaving the rice undisturbed lets the base form a golden, crisp socarrat crust, whereas stirring releases starch and makes it creamy like risotto.
variations: Swap the chicken for 400 g of peeled raw prawns and 200 g of firm white fish, stirring them in for the last 8 minutes of simmering so they stay tender, and use fish or seafood stock for a seafood paella style.
Make it vegetarian by replacing the chicken and chorizo with 1 sliced zucchini, 1 drained can of chickpeas and an extra teaspoon of smoked paprika, and use vegetable stock.
storage: Refrigerate promptly in an airtight container for up to 3 days. Reheat cooked components until steaming hot; keep crisp garnishes separate.

title: Lamb köfte
summary: Chargrilled lamb kofta with cumin, garlic and parsley, served with flatbread and yoghurt.
method: Squeeze the liquid from the grated onion, then mix with the lamb mince, garlic, spices, parsley and salt.
Knead briefly until the mixture holds together, then shape into 12 short oval patties.
Refrigerate the patties on a tray for 15 minutes. Meanwhile, heat a griddle or heavy pan over medium-high heat.
Brush the köfte with olive oil and grill for about 10 minutes, turning every few minutes, until browned and 75°C in the centre.
Rest the köfte for 3 minutes while warming the flatbreads, then serve with tomato, cucumber and yoghurt.

stages.title: Mix and shape
steps: Squeeze excess liquid from grated onion and mix with lamb, garlic, spices, parsley and salt.
Knead briefly until mixture holds together, then form 12 short oval patties.

stages.title: Chill the patties
steps: Place shaped köfte on a tray and refrigerate 15 minutes to firm.
Heat a griddle or heavy pan while the patties chill.

stages.title: Cook thoroughly
steps: Brush köfte lightly with oil and grill over medium-high heat for about 10 minutes, turning every few minutes.
Cook until browned and the centre reaches 75°C for minced meat.

stages.title: Rest and serve
steps: Rest köfte for 3 minutes while warming flatbreads.
Serve with chopped tomato, cucumber and a yoghurt sauce.

tips: Squeeze the grated onion in your fist or a clean tea towel before mixing; the excess juice makes the mince wet and the köfte can slump or fall apart on the grill.
Chill the shaped patties for the full 15 minutes so the lamb fat firms up and the köfte hold their shape instead of sticking to the grates.
Use a probe thermometer and pull the köfte at 75°C: minced lamb must be cooked through, and resting for 3 minutes lets the juices settle so they stay moist.
variations: Swap half the lamb for beef mince for a milder, more budget-friendly köfte that still browns well.
Thread the mixture onto flat metal skewers to make şiş köfte, then serve with charred tomatoes and capsicum and a sumac onion salad.
storage: Refrigerate promptly in an airtight container for up to 3 days. Reheat cooked components until steaming hot; keep crisp garnishes separate.

title: Beef phở
summary: Fragrant beef broth with rice noodles, tender beef, fresh herbs and warming spices.
method: Char the onion and ginger under a hot grill until the edges blacken lightly, then rinse and toast the star anise, cinnamon and cloves in a dry pan over medium heat until fragrant.
Cover the bones or oxtail with water, boil for 5 minutes, then drain and rinse the bones and pot.
Return the bones to the pot with the 1 litre of fresh water (plus extra to cover), the charred aromatics and the spices. Simmer gently for 2 hours, skimming off foam.
Strain the broth, then season with the fish sauce and a little salt until savoury but not too salty.
Cook the rice noodles until tender, then divide between warm bowls and top with the thinly sliced steak.
Pour vigorously boiling broth over the beef until it is cooked through, then serve with bean sprouts, basil and lime.

stages.title: Char the aromatics
steps: Char onion halves and ginger under a hot grill until edges blacken lightly.
Rinse charred surfaces briefly and toast whole spices in a dry pan over medium heat until fragrant.

stages.title: Build the broth
steps: Cover bones with water, boil for 5 minutes, drain and rinse bones and pot to remove impurities.
Add fresh water, aromatics and spices and simmer gently for 2 hours, skimming foam as needed.

stages.title: Strain and season
steps: Strain broth through a fine sieve and discard solids and spent spices.
Season with fish sauce and a little salt until savoury but not overly salty.

stages.title: Assemble bowls
steps: Soak or boil noodles as directed until tender, divide between warm bowls and top with thin beef slices.
Pour vigorously boiling broth over beef, ensuring it cooks through, and serve with herbs, sprouts and lime.

tips: Parboil the bones for 5 minutes and rinse them before the long simmer. This pulls out the blood and impurities that would otherwise cloud the broth and leave a scummy, muddy flavour.

Slice the steak as thinly as you can, ideally after 20 minutes in the freezer to firm it up. Paper-thin slices cook through instantly when the boiling broth hits them and stay tender instead of going grey and chewy.
Keep the broth at a gentle simmer rather than a rolling boil. Hard boiling emulsifies the fat and collagen into the liquid, making the pho cloudy and greasy rather than clear and clean-tasting.
variations: Swap the steak for chicken pho (pho ga): use a whole chicken or chicken carcasses instead of beef bones, simmer for about 1 hour, then shred the meat to top the bowls.
Make a vegetarian version with a broth of charred onion, ginger, daikon, dried shiitake mushrooms and the same spices, then top with fried tofu and bok choy in place of the beef.
storage: Refrigerate promptly in an airtight container for up to 3 days. Reheat cooked components until steaming hot; keep crisp garnishes separate.

title: BBQ pulled pork
summary: Slow-smoked-style shredded pork with a sweet, tangy barbecue glaze and crisp edges.
method: Pat the pork shoulder dry and rub all over with the brown sugar, smoked paprika, garlic powder, onion powder and salt.
Place in a snug lidded roasting dish and pour the apple juice around, not over, the meat.
Cover tightly and roast at 150°C for about 4 hours, until fork-tender. Check occasionally that liquid remains in the base.
Rest the pork 10 minutes, remove excess fat and shred. Mix with the warm cooking juices and BBQ sauce until moist but not soupy.
Toast the burger buns cut-side down until lightly golden, then pile in the pulled pork and add coleslaw if you like.

stages.title: Season the pork
steps: Pat shoulder dry and rub all over with sugar, paprika, garlic powder, onion powder and salt.
Place in a snug lidded roasting dish and pour apple juice around, not over, the meat.

stages.title: Slow roast
steps: Cover tightly and roast at 150°C conventional for about 4 hours.
Check occasionally that liquid remains in the base and cook until pork is fork-tender.

stages.title: Shred and sauce
steps: Rest pork 10 minutes, remove excess fat and shred with two forks.
Mix with warm cooking juices and BBQ sauce until moist but not soupy.

stages.title: Serve
steps: Toast burger buns cut-side down until lightly golden.
Pile in pulled pork and add coleslaw if desired.

tips: Pour the apple juice around the pork, not over it, so the spice rub stays intact and builds a proper bark instead of washing into the liquid.
Leave the pork covered for the whole cook: a tight lid traps steam, which melts the collagen in the shoulder and keeps the meat moist and fork-tender.
Toss the shredded pork in the warm cooking juices before adding the BBQ sauce, as the fat-rich juices carry flavour through the meat and stop the sauce tasting sugary and flat.
variations: Swap the BBQ sauce for a Carolina-style mix of apple cider vinegar, a little brown sugar and chilli flakes for a tangier, thinner finish, and serve with crunchy slaw on the bun.
Make it in a slow cooker: cook on low for 8 hours, then spread the shredded pork on a tray, brush with sauce and grill for 5 minutes to get crisp edges.
storage: Cool promptly; refrigerate pulled pork up to 3 days or freeze up to 3 months. Reheat until steaming hot.

title: Beef bourguignon
summary: Beef slowly braised in red wine with mushrooms, carrots and pearl onions until fork-tender.
method: Pat the beef dry, season, then brown in batches in the olive oil in a heavy casserole over medium-high heat, about 2 to 3 minutes a side until deeply browned.
Remove the beef and fry the bacon until golden. Soften the onion and carrots, then add the garlic and flour and cook 1 minute.
Pour in the wine slowly, scraping the base, then add the stock, thyme, beef and bacon.
Cover and cook at 160°C for about 2½ hours until the beef is fork-tender, adding a little stock halfway if it looks dry.
Brown the mushrooms separately in a hot pan until golden, then stir into the stew for the last 10 minutes. Adjust the seasoning.

stages.title: Brown beef and bacon
steps: Pat beef dry, season, then brown in batches in olive oil in a heavy casserole over medium-high heat, about 2 to 3 minutes a side until deeply browned.
Remove beef and fry bacon until golden, leaving some fat in the pot.

stages.title: Build the braise
steps: Soften chopped onion and carrots, then add garlic and flour and stir 1 minute.
Pour in wine slowly, scraping the base, then add stock, thyme, beef and bacon.

stages.title: Slow cook
steps: Cover and cook at 160°C conventional for about 2½ hours until beef is fork-tender.
Check liquid halfway and add a little stock if it becomes dry.

stages.title: Finish mushrooms
steps: Brown mushrooms separately in a hot skillet to prevent them steaming.
Stir into the stew for the last 10 minutes and adjust seasoning before serving.

tips: Pat the beef dry and brown it in batches: crowding the pot makes the meat steam rather than sear, and you lose the browned base that gives the sauce its depth.
Use a wine you'd happily drink, such as a Pinot Noir or Burgundy-style red. The wine reduces over the long braise, so any harshness or sourness gets concentrated in the sauce.
Brown the mushrooms separately in a hot pan and add them near the end. Cooked in the stew for hours they turn soggy and grey, but this keeps their texture and flavour.
variations: Swap the beef chuck for beef cheeks or oxtail. Their extra collagen makes a silkier, more sticky sauce, but allow an extra 30 to 45 minutes of braising.
Make it a Beef and Guinness-style stew by replacing the red wine with a dark stout and adding a spoonful of tomato paste. Serve with mash or crusty bread for a heartier, maltier dish.
storage: Refrigerate promptly in an airtight container for up to 3 days. Reheat cooked components until steaming hot; keep crisp garnishes separate.

title: Greek lemon potatoes
summary: Roast potatoes infused with lemon, oregano, garlic and olive oil until golden and tender.
method: Heat the oven to 210°C. Cut the potatoes into thick wedges and toss in a roasting dish with the oil, lemon juice, garlic, oregano and salt.
Pour the stock around the potatoes and spread them in a single layer.
Roast for 35–40 minutes, turning once, until tender and most of the liquid has evaporated.
Increase the oven to 230°C, turn the potatoes to expose the pale sides and roast 10–15 minutes more, until golden.
Spoon the pan juices over, taste for salt and serve straight away with extra lemon wedges.

stages.title: Cut and season
steps: Heat oven to 210°C conventional and cut potatoes into even thick wedges.
Toss with olive oil, lemon juice, minced garlic, oregano and salt in a roasting dish.

stages.title: Add stock and roast
steps: Pour stock around potatoes and spread wedges in a single layer.
Roast 35–40 minutes, turning once, until tender and most liquid has evaporated.

stages.title: Crisp the edges
steps: Increase oven to 230°C and turn potatoes to expose pale surfaces.
Roast a further 10–15 minutes until golden, adding only a splash of water if sticking.

stages.title: Finish and serve
steps: Spoon pan juices over the potatoes and taste for salt.
Serve immediately with extra lemon wedges.

tips: Use waxy potatoes such as Desiree or Dutch cream: they hold their shape while absorbing the lemon stock, whereas floury varieties like Russet Burbank can collapse into mush.
Cut wedges to an even thickness so they all finish tender at the same time and the stock reduces evenly around them.
Turn the potatoes so their pale, damp surfaces face up for the final high-heat blast; the surfaces that sat in the liquid are the ones that need to dry out and brown.
variations: Swap half the potatoes for sweet potato wedges and add them for the second roasting stage, since they cook faster and their sweetness balances the sharp lemon.
Stir 1 tbsp of Dijon mustard into the lemon and oil mixture for a tangy, slightly creamy coating, and scatter crumbled feta over the top just before serving.
storage: Refrigerate promptly in an airtight container for up to 3 days. Reheat cooked components until steaming hot; keep crisp garnishes separate.

title: Fluffy banana pancakes
summary: Thick, fluffy banana pancakes with caramelised edges and naturally sweet fruit flavour.
method: Mash the bananas with a fork until mostly smooth, then whisk in the eggs, milk, vanilla and cooled melted butter.
In another bowl, combine the flour, baking powder, sugar and salt.
Fold the wet mixture into the dry just until combined; small lumps are fine.
Heat a lightly buttered nonstick pan over medium-low heat. Cook 60 ml portions for 2–3 minutes until bubbles form, then flip and cook 1–2 minutes until the centres are set.
Keep the cooked pancakes warm under a clean tea towel while you finish the batch.
Serve with sliced banana and yoghurt or maple syrup.

stages.title: Mash bananas
steps: Mash ripe bananas with a fork until mostly smooth, leaving a few small lumps.
Whisk in eggs, milk, vanilla and cooled melted butter.

stages.title: Mix batter
steps: Combine flour, baking powder, sugar and salt in another bowl.
Fold wet ingredients into dry just until combined; small lumps are fine.

stages.title: Cook pancakes
steps: Heat a lightly buttered nonstick skillet over medium-low heat.
Cook 60 ml portions for 2–3 minutes until bubbles form, flip and cook 1–2 minutes until centres are set.

stages.title: Serve warm
steps: Keep cooked pancakes warm under a clean tea towel while finishing the batch.
Serve with sliced banana and yoghurt or maple syrup.

tips: Use bananas with plenty of brown spots: they are sweeter and mash more smoothly, so the pancakes taste of banana without needing extra sugar.
Stop folding while the batter is still a little lumpy. Overmixing develops gluten and makes the pancakes tough and flat instead of fluffy.
Keep the heat at medium-low and wait for bubbles before flipping. The banana sugars caramelise and burn quickly, and a hotter pan browns the outside before the thick centre sets.
variations: Fold 1/3 cup of dark chocolate chips or chopped walnuts into the batter for a banoffee-style stack.
Swap 50 g of the plain flour for wholemeal flour and add 1/2 tsp cinnamon for a nuttier, warmly spiced pancake.
storage: Refrigerate promptly in an airtight container for up to 3 days. Reheat cooked components until steaming hot; keep crisp garnishes separate.

title: Masala dosa with potato filling
summary: Crisp fermented rice-lentil crêpes wrapped around warmly spiced potatoes and onions.
method: Boil the peeled potato chunks until tender, then drain and roughly mash.
Heat 1 tbsp of the oil in a pan over medium heat. Pop the mustard seeds, then soften the onion, chilli, curry leaves and turmeric, about 5 minutes.
Fold the mashed potato into the spiced onion and season with salt. Add a splash of water if dry, so it's moist but not runny.
Heat a nonstick skillet over medium-high heat and lightly oil it. Spread a ladle of dosa batter thinly and cook until golden underneath and the edges lift.
Fill each dosa with the potato mixture and fold. Serve straight away with sambar or a chutney.

stages.title: Cook potato filling
steps: Boil peeled potato chunks until tender, then drain and roughly mash.
Heat 1 tbsp oil over medium heat, pop mustard seeds, add onion, chilli, curry leaves and turmeric, and soften until the onion is translucent, about 5 minutes.

stages.title: Finish filling
steps: Fold mashed potatoes into the spiced onion and season with salt.
Add a splash of water if dry; filling should be moist but not runny.

stages.title: Cook thin dosas
steps: Heat a flat nonstick skillet and lightly oil it, then spread a ladle of batter in a thin spiral.
Cook until the underside is golden and edges lift, adding a few drops of oil around the rim.

stages.title: Fill and fold
steps: Place warm potato mixture along the centre of each dosa.
Fold over and serve immediately with sambar or a chutney.

tips: Wipe the hot pan with a halved onion or a lightly oiled cloth between dosas; this keeps the surface just greased enough for the batter to spread thinly without tearing or sticking.
Spread the batter in quick outward spirals as soon as it hits the pan, because it sets within seconds and a thin, even layer is what gives the crisp, lacy texture.
Mash the potatoes only roughly and let the filling cool slightly before spooning it in; chunky pieces keep some texture and a slightly cooled filling won't soften the crisp dosa.
variations: Make a paneer masala dosa by folding 150 g crumbled paneer through the potato filling with a pinch of garam masala for a more protein-rich breakfast.
Swap half the potato for cooked peas and diced carrot for a veggie-packed filling that suits kids, and leave out the green chilli.
storage: Refrigerate filling up to 3 days and batter according to its label. Cook dosas fresh for crispness.

title: Falafel wraps
summary: Warm flatbread wrapped around crisp falafel, pickles, vegetables and tahini sauce.
ingredients: 150 g Greek yoghurt, mixed with the tahini
method: Pulse the drained, dry soaked chickpeas with the onion, garlic, parsley, coriander, cumin and ground coriander until finely crumbly, not puréed.
Mix in the baking powder, chill for 30 minutes, then press into small, firm patties.
Heat 2 cm oil in a deep pan over medium-high heat to about 175°C. Fry the falafel in batches until deep golden, then drain.
Check the centres are cooked through.
Warm the flatbreads and spread with the tahini and yoghurt mixture.
Fill with falafel, lettuce, tomato and pickles, then roll up tightly.

stages.title: Blend falafel mix
steps: Drain chickpeas soaked overnight and dry thoroughly; do not cook them first.
Pulse with onion, garlic, herbs and spices until finely crumbly, not puréed.

stages.title: Chill and shape
steps: Mix in baking powder and refrigerate the mixture 30 minutes.
Form small compact patties, pressing firmly so they hold together.

stages.title: Fry falafel
steps: Heat 2 cm oil to about 175°C in a deep pan over medium-high heat and fry in batches until deep golden.
Drain on kitchen paper and check centres are cooked through.

stages.title: Build wraps
steps: Warm flatbreads and spread with tahini yoghurt sauce.
Add falafel, lettuce, tomato and pickles and roll tightly.

tips: Use soaked raw chickpeas, not canned or pre-cooked ones. Canned chickpeas hold too much water and turn the mix to mush, so the patties fall apart in the oil.
Pulse the mix to a coarse crumb that clumps when squeezed. Puréeing releases starch and gives dense, pasty falafel instead of a light, crisp-edged centre.
Keep the oil around 175°C and fry in small batches. Hotter oil browns the outside before the centre cooks, and overcrowding drops the temperature so the falafel soak up oil.
variations: Bake instead of frying: brush the patties with oil and bake at 220°C for about 25 minutes, turning once, for a lighter version with a less crisp crust.
Swap half the chickpeas for soaked dried broad beans (fava beans) for a greener, more traditional Egyptian-style falafel with a fluffier centre.
storage: Refrigerate cooked falafel up to 3 days or freeze up to 2 months. Reheat in a hot oven until steaming hot; assemble wraps fresh.

title: Crème brûlée
summary: Smooth vanilla custard beneath a brittle, caramelised sugar crust.
ingredients: 1 vanilla bean or 2 tsp vanilla paste
40 g extra caster sugar for topping
method: Heat the oven to 150°C conventional. Warm the cream and vanilla in a saucepan over low heat until steaming, not boiling, then leave to infuse off the heat for 5 minutes.
Whisk the egg yolks and 80 g caster sugar until combined but not foamy. Slowly whisk in the warm cream, then strain.
Divide the custard among four ramekins in a deep roasting tray. Pour hot water halfway up the ramekins.
Bake for 35–40 minutes, until the edges are set but the centres still wobble.
Cool, then refrigerate for at least 2 hours until cold and firm.
Just before serving, sprinkle the extra caster sugar in thin, even layers and caramelise with a kitchen torch until golden.

stages.title: Heat cream
steps: Heat oven to 150°C conventional and warm cream with vanilla until steaming, not boiling.
Remove from heat and let infuse for 5 minutes.

stages.title: Mix custard
steps: Whisk yolks and 80 g sugar until combined but not foamy.
Slowly pour warm cream into yolks while whisking to avoid scrambling, then strain.

stages.title: Bake in water bath
steps: Divide custard among four ramekins and place in a deep roasting tray.
Pour hot water halfway up ramekins and bake 35–40 minutes until edges set but centres wobble.

stages.title: Chill and caramelise
steps: Cool, then refrigerate at least 2 hours until cold and firm.
Sprinkle thin even sugar layers and caramelise with a kitchen torch immediately before serving.

tips: Pour the hot water into the roasting tray after it's on the oven rack, so you don't slosh water into the custards. The water bath keeps the oven heat gentle and even, which stops the yolks curdling and gives a silky set.

Pull the ramekins out while the centres still wobble like set jelly. The custard keeps cooking from residual heat and firms up fully as it chills, so waiting for a firm centre in the oven leads to a grainy, overcooked texture.
Pat any condensation off the chilled custards with paper towel before sugaring. Moisture on the surface dissolves the sugar into a syrup instead of letting it melt into a glassy, crackly crust.
variations: Swap the vanilla for 2 tbsp of finely grated orange zest and a splash of Grand Marnier, infusing the zest in the warm cream, for a citrus crème brûlée that cuts through the richness.
Infuse the warm cream with 2 tbsp of good loose-leaf Earl Grey tea for 5 minutes, then strain before mixing with the yolks, for a fragrant, bergamot-scented custard.
storage: Refrigerate uncaramelised custards covered up to 2 days. Caramelise just before serving.

title: Apple crumble
summary: Tender baked apples with cinnamon beneath a buttery golden crumble topping.
method: Heat the oven to 190°C. Peel, core and slice the apples, toss with the caster sugar, cinnamon and lemon juice, then spread in a baking dish.
Rub the cold butter into the flour until the mixture looks like coarse crumbs. Stir in the brown sugar and oats, leaving a few buttery clumps.
Scatter the topping over the apples without pressing down. Bake for 30–35 minutes, until golden and the fruit bubbles at the edges.
Rest for 10 minutes so the juices thicken, then serve warm with vanilla ice cream if you like.

stages.title: Prepare fruit
steps: Heat oven to 190°C conventional and peel, core and slice apples evenly.
Toss with caster sugar, cinnamon and lemon juice, then spread in a baking dish.

stages.title: Make crumble topping
steps: Rub cold butter into flour until the mixture looks like coarse crumbs.
Stir in brown sugar and oats, leaving a few larger buttery clumps.

stages.title: Bake until bubbling
steps: Scatter crumble evenly over apples without pressing it down.
Bake 30–35 minutes until topping is golden and fruit bubbles around the edges.

stages.title: Rest and serve
steps: Rest crumble 10 minutes so the juices thicken slightly.
Serve warm with vanilla ice cream.

tips: Use Granny Smith or another firm cooking apple, because they hold their shape and their tartness balances the sweet topping, whereas Pink Lady or Gala can collapse into mush.
Keep the butter cold and leave some pea-sized clumps in the topping, as these melt slowly in the oven and create a crisp, crunchy crumble rather than a flat, greasy layer.
Scatter the crumble over the apples without pressing it down so steam can escape; compacting it traps moisture and makes the underside of the topping soggy.
variations: Swap half the apples for blackberries or rhubarb, adding an extra 2 tbsp of caster sugar for the rhubarb, for a tarter, more colourful filling.
Replace 30 g of the flour with chopped roasted hazelnuts or almond meal for a nuttier, extra crunchy topping.
storage: Refrigerate promptly in an airtight container for up to 3 days. Reheat cooked components until steaming hot; keep crisp garnishes separate.

title: Pastéis de nata
summary: Flaky Portuguese custard tarts with blistered tops and crisp buttery pastry.
method: Heat oven to 240°C. Roll the puff pastry into a tight log, slice into 12 pieces and press each into a greased muffin tin.
Simmer the sugar, water, cinnamon stick and lemon peel for 3 minutes, then remove the cinnamon and peel.
Whisk the flour with a little cold milk, add the remaining milk and heat until lightly thickened.
Slowly whisk the hot syrup into the milk mixture and cool slightly. Whisk in the egg yolks and strain.
Fill the pastry cases three-quarters full. Bake 12–16 minutes until the pastry is crisp and the custard has dark caramelised spots.
Cool in the tins for 10 minutes, then remove and serve warm.

stages.title: Prepare pastry cases
steps: Heat oven to 240°C conventional and roll puff pastry tightly into a log.
Slice into 12 pieces and press each into a greased muffin tin, working from centre outward.

stages.title: Cook syrup and milk
steps: Simmer sugar, water, cinnamon and lemon peel for 3 minutes, then remove aromatics.
Whisk flour with a little cold milk, add remaining milk and heat until lightly thickened.

stages.title: Make custard
steps: Slowly whisk hot syrup into the milk mixture, then let cool slightly.
Whisk in egg yolks and strain to remove lumps before filling pastry shells three-quarters full.

stages.title: Bake until blistered
steps: Bake 12–16 minutes until pastry is crisp and custard tops develop dark caramelised spots.
Cool 10 minutes before removing from tins; serve warm.

tips: Roll the pastry log tightly and press each slice out from the centre with wet thumbs, so the base stays thin and the sides rise into a crisp, flaky cup rather than a doughy one.

Use the hottest oven you can (240°C) and bake near the top: the intense heat blisters the custard and caramelises the sugar into the signature dark spots before the filling overcooks and turns rubbery.
Strain the custard through a fine sieve after adding the yolks, as this catches any cooked egg or flour lumps and gives a silky, smooth filling.
variations: Swap the lemon peel for a strip of orange peel and add a drop of vanilla extract for a softer, more fragrant custard.
Make them Macanese-style by using less sugar syrup and baking at a slightly lower temperature, which gives a lighter, more eggy custard with a golden top and less char.
storage: Refrigerate promptly in an airtight container for up to 3 days. Reheat cooked components until steaming hot; keep crisp garnishes separate.

title: Greek orange and yoghurt cake
summary: Moist Greek yoghurt cake with fresh orange zest and a fragrant citrus syrup.
method: Heat the oven to 180°C and grease a 22 cm round tin. Line the base with baking paper and finely zest the oranges, avoiding the white pith.
Whisk the yoghurt, sugar, eggs, olive oil, vanilla and zest until smooth. Add 80 ml of fresh orange juice and whisk briefly.
Gently fold in the flour and salt until no dry pockets remain.
Pour into the tin and bake for 35–40 minutes, until a skewer in the centre comes out clean.
Cool in the tin for 10 minutes, then turn out onto a rack. Serve with extra yoghurt and a little orange zest.

stages.title: Prepare cake tin
steps: Heat oven to 180°C conventional and grease a 22 cm round cake tin.
Line the base with baking paper and finely zest oranges without white pith.

stages.title: Mix wet ingredients
steps: Whisk yoghurt, sugar, eggs, olive oil, vanilla and orange zest until smooth.
Add 80 ml fresh orange juice and whisk briefly.

stages.title: Fold and bake
steps: Fold in flour and salt gently until no dry pockets remain.
Pour into tin and bake 35–40 minutes until a skewer inserted in centre comes out clean.

stages.title: Cool and serve
steps: Cool in tin 10 minutes, then turn out onto a rack.
Serve with extra yoghurt and a little orange zest.

tips: Zest the oranges before juicing them, and avoid the white pith: it's bitter, while the zest oils carry the fragrant citrus flavour through the crumb.
Fold the flour in gently and stop as soon as no dry pockets remain, because overmixing develops gluten and makes an olive oil cake dense rather than tender.
Use a mild extra virgin olive oil, as a very peppery one can turn bitter against the orange; the oil is what keeps the cake moist for days.
variations: Make it a syrup cake: simmer 100 ml orange juice with 60 g sugar until slightly thickened, then spoon it over the warm cake so it soaks in.
Swap one orange for 2 lemons' worth of zest and juice, and add 2 tbsp poppy seeds for a Greek-style lemon and poppy seed cake.
storage: Refrigerate promptly in an airtight container for up to 3 days. Reheat cooked components until steaming hot; keep crisp garnishes separate.
